# Danish Mohd

> AI product builder. Writes about AI scaling, RAG pipelines, LLM evaluation, and applied machine learning. Previously VP Engineering at Pixis AI. Built and sold SegmentOne (e-commerce personalization). Currently building Pluto Money (AI financial advisor) and an AI-native hedge fund.

## Interactive Explainers

These are in-depth, interactive articles with hands-on visualizations. They are the highest-quality content on this site.

- [The Scaling Laws That Predict Everything](https://supergeek.in/scaling-laws/): How the same power law (y = ax^b) governs biology (Kleiber's law), cities, and neural network performance. Covers Kaplan scaling laws, Chinchilla compute-optimal training, emergent abilities, and what the curves predict for AI timelines. 7 interactive demos.
- [You're Doing RAG Retrieval Wrong](https://supergeek.in/rag-retrieval/): Why RAG pipelines retrieve wrong chunks — semantic dissonance between questions and documents in embedding space. Covers question-to-question matching, domain-specific embeddings, reranking beyond cosine similarity, and empirical threshold setting. 5 interactive demos.
- [Credit Scoring, Explained Plainly](https://supergeek.in/credit-scoring/): How banks decide who gets a loan in 30 seconds. Covers FICO components, Weight of Evidence binning, logistic regression scorecards, XGBoost vs LightGBM comparison, SHAP explainability for regulatory compliance, and PSI drift monitoring. 6 interactive demos.
- [Causal AI in Wealth, Explained](https://supergeek.in/causal-ai/): Why every wealth app confuses correlation with causation. Covers confounders vs colliders, Pearl's causal ladder, causal graphs for SIP cancellation, the engagement trap (collider bias in fintech), and counterfactual reasoning for investor behavior. 6 interactive demos.
- [ML-Based Trading, Explained Plainly](https://supergeek.in/ml-trading/): What actually works in ML trading, what doesn't, and why most quant strategies fail. Covers technical indicators (RSI, MACD, Bollinger), momentum vs mean reversion, overfitting detection, drawdown analysis, SHAP feature importance, and efficient frontier portfolio optimization using real Nifty 50 data. 6 interactive demos.
- [How LLMs Work, Explained Plainly](https://supergeek.in/llm-explainer/): What happens between your prompt and the response. Covers BPE tokenization, embedding spaces, self-attention mechanics, token sampling (temperature, top-k, top-p), the training pipeline (pretraining, SFT, RLHF), and KV cache memory scaling. 6 interactive demos.

## Writing

- [Why RAG fails on time series (and what works instead)](https://supergeek.in/agentic-rag-pipeline-for-time-series-analysis/): Why standard RAG breaks on temporal data, how agentic architectures route to specialized sub-agents, and how time series foundation models (TimesFM, Chronos-2, Lag-Llama) are changing forecasting.
- [Why LLMs forget your instructions (and what actually fixes it)](https://supergeek.in/reduce-forgetfulness-in-llm-instructions/): The U-shaped attention curve, context rot across 18 models, KV cache competition, Writing in the Margins, and practical fixes: instruction pinning, structured prompts, compaction, multi-agent delegation, prompt caching.
- [When AI does its own research](https://supergeek.in/the-ai-scientist/): From $15 papers to peer-reviewed publications. AI Scientist v1/v2 (Sakana), Google AI Co-Scientist (validated drug candidates), AI-Researcher (NeurIPS Spotlight), AlphaProof/Gemini Deep Think (IMO Gold), Ai2 AutoDiscovery, and the state of automated scientific discovery.
- [Why LLMs can't write long (and what breaks the ceiling)](https://supergeek.in/ai-output-limit-solution-agentwrite/): Why LLMs hit output length limits despite million-token context windows. AgentWrite plan-then-generate pipeline, LongWriter-6k dataset (ICLR 2025), Chain of Agents, Recursive Language Models, and the training data bottleneck.
- [Measuring whether your RAG actually works](https://supergeek.in/evaluate-rag-pipelines/): The RAG Triad (context relevance, faithfulness, answer relevance), RAGAS, ARES (Stanford), DeepEval, FaithJudge (EMNLP 2025), LLM-as-a-Judge, MTRAG multi-turn benchmark, and CI/CD quality gates for production RAG.
